question.value: Whether the glycine isomer glycolamide is present in the hot molecular core G358.93-0.03 MM1 and how its abundance compares to chemically related amides (formamide and acetamide) across environments.

evidence.quote: Here we report the tentative detection of glycolamide in a hot molecular core, G358.93-0.03 MM1, using ALMA 1 mm observations.
To explore whether amino-acid-related chemistry extends into these protostellar environments, we investigate the presence of GA in the HMC G358.93-0.03 MM1 (hereafter G358.93 MM1)

This work makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2019.1.00768.S.

findings_qualitative.value: syn-glycolamide is tentatively detected in the hot molecular core G358.93-0.03 MM1 through seven clean spectral features comprising 17 transitions.

evidence.quote: Within this framework, GA is identified toward G358.93 MM1 through seven clean spectral features (Fig. [2](#fig:2)), six of which are detected above the 3$\sigma$ level and three above 5$\sigma$ level.
We therefore regard the identification as tentative.

findings_qualitative.value: The spatial distribution of glycolamide emission is compact and coincident with the formamide, acetamide, and 1 mm continuum peaks.

evidence.quote: The newly obtained GA map is compact and coincident with both the FA and AA emission peaks as well as the continuum maximum.

findings_qualitative.value: The FA/GA and AA/GA abundance ratios in G358.93 MM1 are similar to those in the quiescent molecular cloud G+0.693-0.027, indicating a chemically connected amide network across environments.

evidence.quote: The abundance ratios FA/GA and AA/GA in G358.93-0.03 MM1 closely resemble those measured in the molecular cloud G+0.693-0.027.

findings_qualitative.value: Current astrochemical models systematically overpredict the abundance of glycolamide by at least an order of magnitude relative to acetamide compared to observations.

evidence.loc: Comparison with other sources and chemical models
evidence.quote: While models (cite: 2020ApJ...899...65S; 2022ApJS..259....1G) tend to produce GA at levels comparable to or exceeding AA, observations of both G358.93 MM1 and G+0.693-0.027 show it to be at least one order of magnitude lower than AA (cite: 2023ApJ...953L..20R).

claims.hypothesis: The glycine isomer syn-glycolamide can endure or form in warm, dense hot molecular core environments associated with massive star formation.
claims.experiment: Searched for syn-glycolamide transitions in ALMA Band 7 (~1 mm) spectra of G358.93-0.03 MM1 using a full-source LTE model in GILDAS CLASS/Weeds and rotational diagram analysis.
claims.result: Seven unblended spectral features (17 transitions, E_u = 108-389 K) were identified, yielding N_t(GA) = (5.3 +/- 1.1) x 10^14 cm^-2, T_ex = 102 +/- 20 K, and an H2-relative abundance of (6.8 +/- 2.0) x 10^-11.
claims.finding: syn-glycolamide is tentatively detected in G358.93-0.03 MM1, extending its known occurrence to warm protostellar environments, though broader bandwidth is needed for firm confirmation.

evidence.quote: Within this framework, GA is identified toward G358.93 MM1 through seven clean spectral features (Fig. [2](#fig:2)), six of which are detected above the 3$\sigma$ level and three above 5$\sigma$ level.

However, given the limited bandwidth ($\sim$8 GHz), the modest number of securely detected transitions, and the high line density of this warm HMC, a coincidental assignment cannot be excluded with the confidence required for a firm detection claim.

claims.hypothesis: Glycolamide is chemically linked to formamide and acetamide via shared formation pathways and environments across interstellar and protostellar regimes.
claims.experiment: Derived LTE column densities and moment 0 maps for formamide, acetamide, and glycolamide in G358.93-0.03 MM1 and compared abundance ratios with G+0.693-0.027.
claims.result: GA, FA, and AA emissions are spatially coincident with the 1 mm continuum peak, and the abundance ratios AA/GA (~16.6 +/- 4.8) and FA/GA (~32.3 +/- 10.9) closely match those in G+0.693-0.027.
claims.finding: Amides share related formation environments and analogous precursor-based chemical networks across quiescent and hot-core regimes.

evidence.quote: The newly obtained GA map is compact and coincident with both the FA and AA emission peaks as well as the continuum maximum.

evidence.loc: Chemical linkages of GA with FA and AA
evidence.quote: The similarity of the FA/GA and AA/GA ratios between G358 MM1 and G+0.693-0.027 (cite: 2023ApJ...953L..20R; 2023MNRAS.523.1448Z) suggests that analogous amide-forming networks may operate across both quiescent and hot-core regimes.

claims.hypothesis: Current astrochemical models accurately reproduce the relative abundances of glycolamide, acetamide, and formamide in hot molecular cores.
claims.experiment: Compared observed FA, AA, and GA abundances and ratios in G358.93-0.03 MM1 and G+0.693-0.027 with astrochemical model predictions from Sahu et al. 2020 and Garrod et al. 2022.
claims.result: Models predict GA abundances comparable to or exceeding AA, whereas observed GA abundances are at least one order of magnitude lower than AA (AA/GA ~ 16.6 in G358.93 MM1).
claims.finding: Current astrochemical networks systematically overproduce GA, indicating overestimated formation efficiency or missing destruction pathways.

evidence.loc: Comparison with other sources and chemical models
evidence.quote: The most striking discrepancy arises for GA, whose observed abundance is systematically lower than predicted by current astrochemical models.

evidence.loc: Comparison with other sources and chemical models
evidence.quote: While models (cite: 2020ApJ...899...65S; 2022ApJS..259....1G) tend to produce GA at levels comparable to or exceeding AA, observations of both G358.93 MM1 and G+0.693-0.027 show it to be at least one order of magnitude lower than AA (cite: 2023ApJ...953L..20R).

why_this_data.value: G358.93 MM1 is the brightest submillimetre source in G358.93-0.03 and exhibits exceptionally line-rich spectra and a chemically diverse inventory of prebiotic and amide-related molecules.

evidence.quote: MM1 exhibits exceptionally line-rich spectra and a chemically diverse inventory, including prebiotic or amide-related molecules
This chemical richness makes G358.93 MM1 an ideal testbed to investigate GA and its potential linkage to other amides.

why_this_method.value: Spectra were extracted from slightly offset positions to mitigate severe Doppler broadening and line blending at the continuum peak; only T_ex and N_t were left free in LTE fitting to reduce parameter degeneracy; NH2 13CHO was used because parent FA is optically thick.

evidence.loc: Spectroscopic inputs and local thermodynamic equilibrium modeling
evidence.quote: To reduce parameter degeneracy, only $T_{\rm ex}$ and $N_{\rm t}$ were treated as free parameters

evidence.loc: Spectroscopic inputs and local thermodynamic equilibrium modeling
evidence.quote: To mitigate this issue, spectra were extracted from slightly offset positions (Fig. [1](#fig:1) (b)), where most of the GA lines are less affected by blending and display clean Gaussian profiles with a high signal-to-noise ratios.

Because the FA lines are substantially optically thick, yielding an unrealistically low apparent $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 3.1, the optically thin $^{13}$C isotopologue was used to infer the total FA column density $N_{\rm t}$(FA)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Extracting spectra at the continuum peak (rejected due to severe Doppler broadening and line blending)

evidence.loc: Spectroscopic inputs and local thermodynamic equilibrium modeling
evidence.quote: Although line intensities peak near the continuum maximum, a detailed line-by-line inspection revealed that most GA transitions in this region suffer from significant blending with neighboring species, making reliable identification and fitting particularly challenging.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using parent NH2CHO lines directly for total FA column density (rejected because parent lines are optically thick with apparent 12C/13C = 3.1)

evidence.quote: Because the FA lines are substantially optically thick, yielding an unrealistically low apparent $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C ratio of 3.1, the optically thin $^{13}$C isotopologue was used to infer the total FA column density $N_{\rm t}$(FA)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Automated image-domain continuum subtraction using STATCONT (tested as an alternative to manual UV-domain CASA uvcontsub; yielded ~30% lower N_t(GA) and slightly higher rms of ~1.65 K)

evidence.loc: STATCONT-based continuum subtraction and LTE modeling of GA
evidence.quote: Notably, the column density derived from the STATCONT-based analysis is approximately 30% lower than that from the CASA-based analysis ($5.3\times10^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$).

limitations_admitted.value: Limited bandwidth (~8 GHz), modest number of securely detected transitions (7 features), and high line density mean coincidental line blending cannot be excluded, making the GA detection tentative.

evidence.quote: However, given the limited bandwidth ($\sim$8 GHz), the modest number of securely detected transitions, and the high line density of this warm HMC, a coincidental assignment cannot be excluded with the confidence required for a firm detection claim.

limitations_admitted.value: Uncertainties are affected by line blending, baseline effects, and simplifying LTE assumptions.

evidence.loc: Spectroscopic inputs and local thermodynamic equilibrium modeling
evidence.quote: Because the uncertainties are dominated not only by the fitting procedure, but also by line blending, baseline effects, and the simplifying assumptions of the LTE model, we adopted a conservative uncertainty of 20% for the derived $T_{\rm ex}$ and $N_{\rm t}$ values.

limitations_admitted.value: With only two GA detections to date, conclusions on formation mechanisms remain preliminary.

evidence.loc: Chemical linkages of GA with FA and AA
evidence.quote: Nevertheless, with only two confirmed GA detections to date, any conclusions regarding its precise formation mechanisms remain preliminary.

referee_caveats_inferred: Internal inconsistency in reported GA abundance relative to H2: the abstract reports (1.7 +/- 0.2) x 10^-10, whereas Table 1 reports (0.7 +/- 0.2) x 10^-10 and the Conclusions report (6.8 +/- 2.0) x 10^-11 (the latter two match 5.3e14 / 7.82e24 = 6.78e-11).
The exact coordinates and aperture size of the offset extraction position are only indicated visually in Fig. 1b and not given numerically in the text.
The STATCONT continuum subtraction yields a 30% lower GA column density and reduces the number of >3 sigma features from six to five, highlighting sensitivity of weak features to baseline treatment.
